meta: Part 4 of "Inside AI's brain". In part 3 we built the machine: pieces, the map of meaning, attention. But a new machine knows nothing. This video shows what AI reads and how it learns.
prompt: How up to date is your knowledge?

muc.title: A brain just put together
muc.text: We have the machine: cutting into pieces, the map of meaning, attention. But when it's just built, it knows nothing at all.

muc.title: Reading a whole library
muc.text: Then people let it read. A huge amount of text: web pages, books, articles, even computer code. More than one person could read in a thousand lifetimes.

muc.title: Learning by guessing words
muc.text: The way it learns is simple: hide the next word and make it guess. If it's wrong, it adjusts a little. Repeat billions of times, and it picks up grammar, facts and even how to reason.

muc.title: The cutoff date
muc.text: But the reading has to stop on a certain day, called the cutoff date. AI knows nothing about what happened after that day.

muc.title: What about the latest news?
muc.text: So if you ask about today's gold price, a new law or this week's news, AI may answer with old information, and still sound very sure.

muc.title: Ask for the cutoff date
muc.text: Ask AI "how up to date is your knowledge?". For news, prices and new rules, turn on web search or paste a source for AI to read.

muc.title: It can only continue sentences
muc.text: After reading the whole library, AI only knows how to continue a sentence, not how to answer questions. So how did it become a polite assistant? Part five has the answer.
